blinding_guess.why: validate_trajectory_msg (src/joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:1362-1366) computes the trajectory end time by summing time_from_start over all points, whereas the definition and trajectory.cpp:158 treat time_from_start as an offset from the trajectory start; the check that rejects trajectories ending in the past therefore uses a wrong end time. Also: action goal path_tolerance/goal_tolerance/goal_time_tolerance are never read (tolerances come only from parameters via get_segment_tolerances), although doc/userdoc.rst says goals may specify them; and goals whose last point has nonzero velocities are rejected by default (allow_nonzero_velocity_at_trajectory_end default false, warned at lines 61-68).

notes: Action name: the code builds it as std::string(get_node()->get_name()) + "/follow_joint_trajectory" (relative name resolved in the node namespace); the 'panda_arm_controller' node name is supplied at load time and is not in the snapshot, so the declares entry uses the packet element name with the hard-coded suffix and the type from the code. msg_type strings use the packet's pkg/Type convention; the ROS 2 IDL name of the action is control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory. QoS: the action server uses the rcl_action default server options (cited from rcl_action/rmw defaults for iron, not from a fetched file); the status sub-topic is transient_local while goal/result/cancel services and feedback are volatile; deadline not set (RMW default, recorded null). The msg/field ports are consumed through two channels with different QoS: the action goal (goal service, reliable/volatile by default) and the ~/joint_trajectory subscription created with rclcpp::SystemDefaultsQoS() (src line 789; reliability/durability SYSTEM_DEFAULT, resolved by the RMW implementation, not in the snapshot); which channel the pairing uses cannot be determined from the code, so their qos is null. rate_hz null: no publish rate is set for these elements; action_monitor_rate (default 20.0 Hz, params yaml line 67-75) sets the goal-handle monitoring timer period, not a port rate. Definition hashes are sha256_normalised proxies over files fetched at tags 5.0.0 of ros2/common_interfaces and ros-controls/control_msgs, taken as the iron release tags; the tag-to-distro mapping was not verified (listing tags was outside the allowed sources). Fetched files were cached in the session scratchpad only to run definition_hash.py on them. The sha256 of JointTrajectory.msg does not cover the nested JointTrajectoryPoint definition. Other interfaces not in the packet: ~/joint_trajectory subscription, ~/controller_state publisher (control_msgs/JointTrajectoryControllerState), <node_name>/query_state service (control_msgs/QueryTrajectoryState). exclusive token is the verbatim expression naming the claimed command interfaces; the concrete joint and interface names come from parameters at run time.
